text:
morgan: Quick Q — I'm updating the Terraform that switches the model-proxy Service from ClusterIP -> headless + targeting NLB targetGroup (targetType=ip). Before I open the PR: any obvious TLS/healthcheck gotchas? planning to keep TLS passthrough at the NLB and terminate at the pod.

jihee: curious why headless for NLB? we usually use NodePort w/ targetType=instance or normal ClusterIP for ALB. headless + ip targets can be ok but health checks and readiness interplay is fiddly.

sam: with headless + targetType=ip the k8s service doesn't create a classic LB. Terraform aws_lb_target_group needs correct port & healthcheck protocol. If you're terminating TLS at pod, healthcheck should be tcp (or https if sidecar terminates). Also ensure pods report readiness quickly or they won't be registered.

caroline: also watch ExternalTrafficPolicy. If you want client IP preserved (we do for request attribution), set service.spec.externalTrafficPolicy=Local. But that requires kube-proxy/nodeport + nodePort on nodes to receive traffic. headless -> ip targets bypass node ports (targets are pod IPs). So client IP preservation semantics change.

morgan: ah ok. Our requirement is to preserve source IP for downstream logging and auth. we already have a sidecar that assumes original src ip. So maybe headless+ip won't keep the client ip — is that correct?

sam: correct — NLB with ip targets preserves client IP if target receives the connection directly (it will have client source). But because we rely on kube-proxy for some flows, double-check network path. For ip targets it hits pod ENI, so you should see client IP. But the nodePort+externalTrafficPolicy Local approach is different. TL;DR: ip targets -> should preserve src IP.

jihee: worth testing in staging. also secrets: gateway has TLS secret in namespace infra-ingress currently bound to Gateway. If we switch to terminating at pod, you need to mount TLS certs into the workload or use cert-manager with SecretMirror. We can't keep the same Kubernetes Secret used by Gateway without copying/mirroring.

morgan: good point. plan was to keep certs in k8s secret and mount to deployment. we have a Vault-based rotation job that writes to k8s secret. will that break Gateway binding?

caroline: Gateway uses typed references to secrets e.g., SecretRef in TLSRoute / Gateway. If the secret gets rotated, both Gateway and pods see updated secret if it's same secret. But if you mirror/separate secrets, rotation needs to update both. prefer using single canonical secret in infra namespace and mount it into pod via projected volume + RBAC read.

sam: small terraform snippet for NLB target group we're planning to add (FYI):
```hcl
resource "aws_lb_target_group" "model_proxy" {
  name     = "rg-model-proxy-${var.env}"
  port     = 443
  protocol = "TCP"
  target_type = "ip"
  health_check {
    protocol = "TCP"
    port     = "traffic-port"
    interval = 30
  }
}
```

morgan: thx. one more: health check path — since we're using tcp healthchecks there is no HTTP path. that's fine for grpc. but readinessProbe on pod should match. current readiness is HTTP /ready on port 8080; we need a tcp listener on 443 that proxies to app.

jihee: maybe switch readiness to tcp check on the pod for consistency (or add a small sidecar that answers on 443). otherwise NLB may mark target healthy while pod not ready to serve TLS.

infra-bot: Heads-up: any infra change touching load balancers will trigger a manual review and a 1-hour maintenance window for prod. Please add the tag `infra-review-required` to the PR.

caroline: +1 on infra-bot. also update the runbook with rollback steps: reverting target_group type and re-creating old ALB if needed.

morgan: great, I'll put together a PR with: headless svc + ip target TG, tcp healthcheck, secret mount plan, and a staging test matrix. tagging @jihee @sam for review. I'll add infra-review-required. Thanks all :thumbsup:
